title: Commit-safeguard fence for Optimize suggestions with staged gates and approval lattice
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a transactionally safe commit fence and staged rollout orchestration for Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching/caching/quantization configs). Goal: allow high-confidence automated applies while guaranteeing fast, observable, and reversible rollback when service quality or SLOs deviate. This ticket implements the core enforcement layer for gating, multi-metric canaries, approval handoffs, and an ops-facing rollback playbook.
acceptance_criteria: A centralized commit-fence service accepts a suggestion, validates policy rules, and emits a staged rollout plan
Rollout plans support N stages with percent traffic split, simulated-load checks, and time-based holds
Canary health checks evaluate latency P95, error-rate, and embedding similarity regression with configurable thresholds
Automatic pause + rollback triggers on any threshold breach and records causality in audit logs
Approval workflow integrates with Console (approval UI) and Slack notifications and enforces two-step approvals for >10% cost-impact changes
All actions produce links to supporting artifacts (sim runs, diffed dashboards) and a single-click revert in Console
End-to-end tests that simulate degraded canary behavior and validate rollback sequence pass in CI
tasks: Design commit-fence API contract (POST /suggestions/:id/commit -> plan) and rollout schema (stages[], metrics[], gates[])
Implement staged rollout scheduler in runtime-orchestrator service with feature-flag toggle
Add canary evaluation module: compute baseline windows, run significance test for token-level quality regression
Create approval connector: Console approval UI, Slack workflow, and webhook to block automatic progression
Integrate audit trail: store commit decisions, metric snapshots, and PR/Confluence links in a secure event store
Author ops rollback playbook and include automated remediation scripts in repo (scripts/revert_optimize.sh)
Add CI sim harness that replays sampled traffic and asserts no more than X% quality degradation during canary
notes: Motivation: Customers adopting Optimize want unit-cost wins but TCO risk if a batching/cache setting regresses latency or correctness. We need automation that reduces manual toil while minimizing blast radius.
Trade-offs discussed: conservative default stage sizes (1%, 5%, 25%) slow time-to-value but reduce risk; team prefers parameterized defaults with org-level policy overrides.
Quality signals: combine infra metrics (P95, CPU/GPU load), functional checks (embedding cosine drift, top-k rerank precision delta), and user-facing KPIs when available.
Decision: use two independent stop conditions (infra SLO breach OR model-quality regression) to trigger rollback. Both are required to be auditable.
We will reuse existing rollout framework pieces from ENG-30844 where applicable but must add transactional commit fencing to ensure atomic metadata + runtime config activation.

Preliminary perf results (internal sim): a 5-stage rollout with simulated 0.8x batching saw cost savings with no P95 increase in 92% of runs. Full sim report: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPT/Sim-Results-ENG-47259

Related incident learnings: INC-2025-03-latency-spike influenced the need for faster automatic halting and clearer operator runbooks. See incident postmortem: https://drive.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2025-03-postmortem.pdf
